cards.explanation: The answer is Baal. Hosea 13:1 says Ephraim was exalted in Israel, “But he incurred guilt through Baal, and he died.” When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling. I think that's a sobering turn, friends.

The answer is True. Hosea 13:2 says the idols are made skillfully from their silver, “…all of them the work of craftsmen.” So these weren't rough lumps of metal. A lot of careful work went into them, and the text calls the making of them sin.

The answer is that they vanish. Morning mist, early dew that vanishes, chaff blown from a threshing floor, and smoke through an open window all pass away (Hosea 13:3). The LORD says that's what the idol makers will be like. Four pictures, one message, and nobody can say it didn't get through.

The answer is wilderness. The LORD says, “I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of drought.” (Hosea 13:5) He says He is the LORD their God ever since the land of Egypt (Hosea 13:4). Dry land, and He knew them there.

The answer is that they forget the LORD. Hosea 13:6 says, “When they had pasture, they became satisfied; when they were satisfied, their hearts became proud, and as a result they forgot Me.” Look at the steps in that verse: pasture, satisfied, proud, forgot. Full bellies can make the heart drift.

The answer is a bear. The LORD says, “Like a bear robbed of her cubs I will attack them…” (Hosea 13:8) That makes three animals so far: lion, leopard and bear. This is a stern warning, friends, and I'll leave the animals to say it.

The answer is that they are against their helper. The LORD says, “You are destroyed, O Israel, because you are against Me…” and then names Himself as their helper (Hosea 13:9). So the trouble is that they stood against the One who was helping them. I think that's a hard thing to hear. Look at who He calls Himself even then.

The answer is False. Hosea 13:11 says, “So in My anger I gave you a king, and in My wrath I took him away.” He gave the king in anger, not as a reward. The people had said, “Give me a king and princes…” (Hosea 13:10), and I'd call that a request to think twice about.

The answer is that he fails to present himself at birth. Labor pains come, “…but he is an unwise son. When the time arrives, he fails to present himself at the opening of the womb.” (Hosea 13:13) It's a picture of an unwise son who doesn't show up when the time comes. Ouch.

The answer is ransom from the power of Sheol, a promise right in the middle of the warnings. The LORD says, “I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from Death.” (Hosea 13:14) Ransom and redeem are big words. That's a big promise, so hold onto it, friends.
The answer is the LORD. Hosea 13:15 says, “…an east wind will come—a wind from the LORD rising up from the desert.” This wind doesn't just happen by chance. It comes from Him.

The answer is True. Hosea 13:15 says, “…an east wind will come…” and then, “His fountain will fail, and his spring will run dry.” Ephraim may flourish among his brothers, but the verse says that wind is a wind from the LORD rising up from the desert. The same verse adds that the wind will plunder his treasury of every precious article.
The answer is his treasury. Hosea 13:15 says, “The wind will plunder his treasury of every precious article.” Every precious article, not just a few. That's a whole lot of emptying.

The answer is that she rebelled against her God. Hosea 13:16 says, “Samaria will bear her guilt because she has rebelled against her God.” The rest of that verse is very heavy, friends. Rebellion against her God is the reason it states.
